errors.text: The proposed dominant yield mechanism is solute-friction-controlled thermal activation, whereas the target mechanism is abrupt Shockley-partial nucleation at vacancy clusters or locally disordered atoms.

The hypothesis introduces deformation twinning and FCC-to-HCP transformation as secondary carriers, but the target reports no twinning and only stacking-fault-induced local HCP-like signatures without a bulk phase transformation.

The intervention uses experimental strain rates of approximately 10^-4 to 10^3 s^-1 instead of reconstructing the molecular-dynamics regime of 10^8 to 10^10 s^-1, so its rate-sensitivity claim is tested in a fundamentally different kinetic regime.

The cited evidence predominantly concerns different compositions, nanowire geometries, refractory HEAs, corrosion, or high-temperature creep and does not directly establish the proposed mechanism in bulk single-crystal FeNiCrMn.
